mainEntity.name: Can you guarantee a number of links per month?

acceptedAnswer.text: We agree a target in the scope. Outreach depends on editors, so we do not promise an exact count and we say so up front.

mainEntity.name: Do you use private blog networks?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We do not use link networks, and we avoid practices that search engines treat as schemes.

mainEntity.name: What do I get in the report?

acceptedAnswer.text: A log of live links with the site, page, date and anchor, plus notes on outreach in progress.

mainEntity.name: Will my client know MMC is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to tell them. We sign an NDA, work under your brand, send deliverables in your format and do not contact your clients unless you ask us to.

acceptedAnswer.text: Share the client, the market and the target pages. We sign the NDA and return a target list for your approval.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label link building is outreach and content placement carried out for your client's website while you present it as your own work. We research targets, pitch editors, place content and send a log of every link, so your SEO retainers have an authority workstream behind them.
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) delivers link building for agencies and works behind your brand. You own the client relationship; we do the work.

blocks.h: How we approach white-label link building
paras: We avoid link schemes and bulk networks. Placements come from outreach to real sites with real audiences, and each is chosen for relevance to your client's market.

stages.breaks: Targets are picked by size, not by fit.
stages.why: A big site that does not cover your client's topic adds little and can look odd.
stages.does: Every site is scored for topic and audience first, and you approve the list before an editor hears from us.

stages.breaks: One pitch template goes to every editor.
stages.why: Editors can tell, and your client's name gets linked with spam.
stages.does: Each pitch is written around an angle the editor's readers would use, sent from an address you have approved.

stages.breaks: The link lands where nobody reads.
stages.why: A link in a footer or on a thin page earns little and is hard to defend to the client.
stages.does: We aim for placements inside useful content, and tell you when a placement misses the standard we agreed.

stages.breaks: Anchor text repeats and looks forced.
stages.why: Repeating one phrase is easy to spot and a risk to the client's site.
stages.does: Anchors are varied and natural, set against a plan for the client, and checked before a link goes live.

stages.breaks: You cannot show the client what was done.
stages.why: Without a record, a retainer for authority looks like nothing happened.
stages.does: Every link goes into a log with date, page, anchor and status, in a format you can drop into your report.
